title: The Dow Falls 335 Points as Corporate News Turns Bad
text:
The Dow Falls 335 Points as Corporate News Turns Bad By Jan. 28, 2019 11:48 a.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
Moody Monday . Markets were still stuck in the red at midday on Monday, as earnings weren’t able to provide the lift they have offered in recent days. Downbeat reports have left investors nervous about upcoming results from major players like Apple (ticker: AAPL) and Microsoft (MSFT) later this week. Even without the latest news, there was plenty to worry about, including concern over slowing global economic growth and a dearth of progress in resolving the U.S.-China trade war. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.3%, while the S&P 500 was off 1.1%.
Midday Movers
Alaska Air Group (ALK) rose 2.6% to $65.15 after Macquarie upgraded it to Outperform .
Nvidia (NVDA) fell 13.5% to $138.55 after lowering its fourth-quarter forecast. The chip maker now expects revenue of $2.2 billion, down from $2.7 billion and below the $2.71 billion analysts were expecting. It also trimmed its gross-margin guidance, citing macroeconomic deterioration in China and lower demand for chips from cryptocurrency miners.
PG&E (PCG) was halted after popping on reports that investors are offering $4 billion in capital to keep the utility from filing for bankruptcy.
Wayfair (W) was up 2.6% to $104.90 after Credit Suisse upgraded it to Outperform.
